title: A withdrawn test cell owes nothing and hides nothing
action: testCellDebt has two linked defects around a dropped test cell, found live when this feature's own close-door refused on a cell that had been deliberately withdrawn. In the test-class branch (state.mjs around :2580-2602) the counter is incremented BEFORE the status check, so a dropped cell (a) counts toward testCellCount and therefore suppresses the 'missing' kind, and (b) simultaneously lands in offenders through the `cell.status !== 'capped'` arm, reported as 'not capped'. A cell that was explicitly dropped is withdrawn work: it owes no coverage and it must not stand in for coverage either. Fix both halves together: skip a dropped test cell entirely — neither counted nor an offender — so that a feature which drops its only test cell falls through to the 'missing' kind rather than passing. That ordering is what keeps the fix from becoming an escape hatch: dropping the test cell must never be cheaper than writing it. Do not widen this to any other status; 'open', 'claimed' and 'blocked' are genuinely undischarged work and must keep refusing. This is a bugfix change_class, so red-first: write the failing cases first in packages/bee/tests/test_bee_cli.mjs, run them red once, and keep them. Required cases: a dropped test cell alongside a capped behavior cell yields the 'missing' kind naming the behavior cell, not a 'not green' offender; a dropped test cell alongside a green capped test cell leaves the door open; an open or blocked test cell still refuses. Extend the existing generated door matrix rather than adding a parallel one. This cell owns its regen chain — run the plugin skill-tree render, then the onboarding apply, then the release-manifest write, in that order, before capping.
